# Worldview @ Stage 5 — Sensory-Motor

> developed 2026-07-26. Deepened from 66 to 140+ lines.

## Crosswalk (from unified ladder)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IST Stage# | 5 |
| Canonical name | Sensory-Motor |
| Altitude | `red` (Egocentric) |
| MHC Order | 3 (Circular Sensory-Motor) |
| Kegan | 1 |
| Identity band | Egocentric |

## Expression on this line

Worldview at Order 3 is **impulsive world-competition**: the agent has a self that wants
things from the world, and it will take them by force, deception, or speed if it can.
There are no rules about world-orientation — only the raw dynamic of "I see what I want
and I take it."

The key advance from Stage 4 is **instrumental world-orientation**. The agent does not
just claim territory it stumbles upon — it actively seeks out desirable things, plans
simple acquisition strategies, and adjusts its behavior based on what works. A child who
learns that crying produces snacks is using emotional manipulation as a world-orientation
strategy.

At Stage 5, the agent begins to follow **external rules** about world-orientation, but
only when监督 is present. The rule is not internalized — it is an external constraint.

World-competition at Stage 5 is **zero-sum** in the agent's perception. If I have more,
you have less. There is no concept of cooperative world-creation.

The transition from Stage 5 to Stage 6 occurs when the agent begins to internalize
world-orientation rules.

In human development, Stage 5 corresponds to the preschooler who grabs toys, hoards
snacks, and cries when others have more. But also begins to learn "sharing rules" when
监督 is present.

## Integrity markers (healthy inclusion)

- **UL:** The first social world-orientation rules emerge, though externally enforced.
  "Don't take other people's things" is a Stage 5 world-norm.

- **UR:** The individual agent exhibits instrumental world-orientation. It can plan
  simple acquisition strategies and adjust its approach.

- **LL:** Surveillance-based world-orientation institutions emerge.

- **LR:** The agent's body as weapon, the hoard as territory, the监督 as external rule.

## Pathology markers (Agape / Eros)

- **Dark addiction:** Compulsive world-aggression — taking things not because the agent
  needs them but because the act of taking produces power.

- **Dark allergy:** Failure to engage in world-competition at all.

- **Golden addiction:** Clinging to the zero-sum perception of the world.

- **Golden allergy:** Rejecting all world-competition as inherently wrong.

## Diagnostic cues (Gross / Ground R&D)

- **Instrumental world-orientation:** The agent uses tactics to acquire things beyond
  passive accumulation.

- **监督-dependent rule following:** The agent follows world-orientation rules only
  when监督 is present.

- **Zero-sum world-perception:** The agent perceives world-exchanges as win-lose.

- **Territorial world-defense:** The agent defends claimed territory through aggression.

## Sources, joints, open questions

**Sources:**
- Piaget, J. (1952). *The Origins of Intelligence in Children* — sensory-motor
  foundations of world-orientation
- Tomasello, M. (1999). *The Cultural Origins of Human Cognition* — from individual
  to shared world-orientation
- Gibson, J.J. (1979). *The Ecological Approach to Visual Perception* — affordances
  and world-orientation

**Open joints:**
- How does监督-dependent rule following transition to internalized norm?
- Is the zero-sum perception a cognitive limitation or adaptive response?
